papers.title_en: WaveMark: Robust Wavelet-Domain Image Watermarking for Diffusion Models
papers.authors: Jie Cao, Qi Li, Chaklam Cheong, Yutong Jin, Enze Yu, Zelin Zhang, Jianbing Ni
papers.evidence: 面向扩散模型生成图像的鲁棒小波域水印
papers.tldr: 扩散模型生成的逼真图像需要水印实现溯源，但现有方法易被 SOTA 移除攻击抑制，且几乎不造成感知退化。WaveMark 将消息嵌入扩散模型初始噪声，并在小波域把消息比特的密钥副本分散到空间位置、小波方向与尺度。每个载体聚合四个潜通道系数，通过幅度投影编码随机比特，从而形成显式解码裕度。在 SD2.1 上经 14 种攻击测试，无攻击时比特准确率达 100%，抗 MarkNull 与 MarkNull-A 仍保持超过 88%，图像质量与基线相当。
papers.abstract_en: Image watermarking enables provenance tracing for photorealistic images generated by diffusion models. However, state-of-the-art (SOTA) removal attacks can suppress embedded signals with little perceptual degradation. This vulnerability limits the effectiveness of watermarks for intellectual property protection and misuse attribution. We propose WaveMark, a novel wavelet-domain watermarking method that embeds messages in a diffusion model's initial noise. To support robust recovery from perturbed carriers, WaveMark distributes keyed replicas of message bits across spatial positions, wavelet orientations, and scales. Each carrier groups coefficients from four latent channels and encodes a randomized bit through magnitude projection, providing an explicit decoding margin. We evaluate WaveMark with SD2.1 on SDP and MS-COCO Captions under 14 attacks. WaveMark achieves 100.0% bit accuracy (BA) without attacks, while maintaining image quality comparable to the evaluated baselines. Under SOTA MarkNull and MarkNull-A, it retains over 88% BA, outperforming all baselines.

papers.title_en: EvoKnow: Continual Knowledge Evolution for AI-Generated Image Detection
papers.authors: Zhiheng Peng, Wenwei Jin, Yangshi Ge, Siyu Xia, Jiawei Li, Xu Tang
papers.evidence: 跨生成模型的AI生成图像持续检测
papers.tldr: AI生成图像检测器常依赖固定生成器域训练，新模型涌现后难以维护，且历史样本回放成本高、参数更新易覆盖旧取证知识。EvoKnow将连续检测建模为取证知识演化：保留基础域共享取证基，增量添加隔离残差专家，并用闭式更新的AIR路由器检索专家。在GenImage非基础生成器上平均准确率达96.70%，Chameleon上达94.48%；严格无回放协议下阶段准确率96.32%、遗忘率4.32%。该框架实现了跨生成器泛化、少样本扩展与长时连续适应。
papers.abstract_en: AI-generated image detectors are commonly trained on fixed generator domains and become difficult to maintain as new generative models emerge. Continual adaptation is challenging because replaying historical generated images is costly, whereas updating shared parameters with limited current-domain data can overwrite prior forensic knowledge. We propose EvoKnow, a replay-free framework that formulates continual AI-generated image detection as forensic knowledge evolution. EvoKnow preserves a shared forensic basis learned from base domains, incrementally adds isolated residual experts for complementary generator-relevant evidence, and retrieves expertise through an Analytical Incremental Router (AIR) updated in closed form from current-stage generated images and accumulated sufficient statistics. Experiments demonstrate effective cross-generator generalization, few-shot expansion, and long-horizon continual adaptation. With ten generated images per arriving generator, EvoKnow achieves 96.70% average accuracy on non-base GenImage generators and 94.48% accuracy on Chameleon without target-benchmark adaptation. Under a strict replay-free continual learning protocol, EvoKnow achieves state-of-the-art continual learning performance, attaining 96.32% mean stage-wise accuracy and 4.32% average forgetting.
